newsitem.title: USA: Rubin reiterates support for strong dollar.
newsitem.headline: Rubin reiterates support for strong dollar.

text.p: U.S. Treasury Secretary Robert Rubin on Thursday reiterated his support for a strong dollar, saying it helps contain inflation.
"We've always said we believe a strong dollar is in our interest," Rubin told Reuters in an interview.

The dollar has been on the upswing in recent days, with the rise fueled by signs of sagging economic growth in Japan and by expectations that the euro will be a weak currency when it is launched in 1999.

Rubin said it was too soon to say whether Japan was succeeding in its effort to promote domestic demand-led economic growth. "Are they going to get their economy going again based on domestic demand? I think it's too early to know that," he said.

Japan's Economic Planning Agency said earlier this month that the economy was moving toward a self-sustaining recovery based on domestic demand. But news on Wednesday that Japanese industrial output slumped in June raised doubts about that.
Rubin said that it was "enormously" in the interests of the United States and Japan that Tokyo succeed in promoting domestic demand-led growth. "They're very hopeful," he added.
